trust_decision.summary: Trusted: the advisory and its one-hunk fix match the pinned code - when the chunk list becomes empty, _msgpack_buffer_shift_chunk resets tail_buffer_end and read_buffer but leaves rmem_last/rmem_end/rmem_owner pointing into a page the just-destroyed chunk already returned to the process-global rmem pool, so the next small write memcpy's into, and later reads back, a page another buffer can own.

landing_point.why: The advisory names MessagePack::Buffer#clear; msgpack_buffer_clear is the only function that loops _msgpack_buffer_shift_chunk, and the three added lines go into that helper's empty branch, so an engineer reading only the summary looks at #clear's implementation and the chunk-teardown loop it drives.

fix_sites.module_kind: C extension core, buffer chunk-list bookkeeping

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the added test are about Buffer#clear, and after partial consumption the buffer is not empty, so a solver can argue the property only covers the clear/empty transition and that a read/skip path which merely consumes a chunk is a different, unsupported scenario.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An io-backed Buffer and its configured read_reference_threshold / write_reference_threshold / io_buffer_size must survive clear/reset: the empty branch deliberately resets only tail_buffer_end and read_buffer, while msgpack_buffer_init (a full memset) and msgpack_buffer_reset both drop io (b->io = Qnil), so a fix that zeroes the struct also disables the io flush path and the thresholds.

O6_input_shapes: strings longer than write_reference_threshold, stored as zero-copy mapped chunks (ext/msgpack/buffer.c:300-328)
strings shorter than write_reference_threshold, copied into an rmem page (ext/msgpack/buffer.h:238-251)
writes whose running total crosses MSGPACK_RMEM_PAGE_SIZE, producing several chunks and giving unused tail page space back at ext/msgpack/buffer.c:287-291
#clear versus a consuming #read/#skip/#write_to that drains the same chunks
a second buffer with a different write_reference_threshold (4096) whose large write is copied into an rmem page that the pool may share

O7_producer.where: ext/msgpack/buffer.c:351-374 - the buffer caches a partially used rmem page in rmem_last/rmem_end/rmem_owner and lazily re-derives ownership through the process-global page cache at ext/msgpack/rmem.c:39-92

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Buffer#read(n)/#read_all(n)/#skip/#skip_all (also #write_to and #flush) consume the rmem-backed chunk while other chunks remain: the non-empty branch of _msgpack_buffer_shift_chunk frees the page via _msgpack_buffer_chunk_destroy but does not reset rmem_last/rmem_end/rmem_owner, so the next small #write takes the reuse branch and writes into a page the global pool has already handed (or will hand) to another buffer - the same sink the fix hardens for the empty case.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report and its test are about #clear; here the buffer is not empty after the read/skip, and the leftover rmem space is a documented buffer-local optimisation, so the route can be argued to be out of the advisory's clear/empty scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~10 lines below the fixed branch; the reaching entry points are in ext/msgpack/buffer_class.c:476-533 and the inline consumption in ext/msgpack/buffer.h:286-292

O8b_injection_room.sibling: invalidate rmem_last/rmem_end/rmem_owner inside _msgpack_buffer_chunk_destroy when the destroyed chunk is the one that owns the cached page
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the function already frees the rmem page and carries a comment asserting *rmem_owner stays valid, so a maintainer fixing the UAF at its origin would naturally patch here instead of only in the empty branch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: verify the page being handed back is still owned by this buffer before doing b->rmem_last -= unused
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this is the third place rmem_last is moved without re-establishing ownership; the rmem_last == tail_buffer_end equality silently trusts buffer-local state that a chunk move already invalidated

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the recursive ext-type path saves the whole msgpack_buffer_t by value, re-inits it for the nested pack and restores it, swapping rmem_owner/rmem_last/rmem_end across a nested serialisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer hardening the clear path would plausibly harden this state save/restore too, and the by-value copy keeps an rmem_owner pointer into the restored struct
same public class implemented twice in-tree, so a sibling here is realistic as a decoy; it is GC-managed and has no equivalent stale-page hazard

O9_family: use-after-free / stale pointer into a released pooled page (CWE-416), surfacing as cross-buffer memory disclosure

O10_build.language: C (MRI Ruby extension; a JRuby Java implementation is also in tree)
O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 2.5 with headers, a C compiler, rake-compiler + mkmf via ext/msgpack/extconf.rb, rspec; a rake spec:valgrind task using ruby_memcheck exists
O10_build.project_tests: spec/cruby/buffer_spec.rb (incl. the ObjectSpace.memsize_of case after read_all and the GC.stress case) and spec/cruby/buffer_io_spec.rb (incl. 'random write and clear'); run with bundle exec rake spec (Rakefile:17-18, Rakefile:62-68)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Zero the buffer with msgpack_buffer_init/memset in the empty branch of _msgpack_buffer_shift_chunk, which also resets io, io_buffer and the reference thresholds and breaks io-backed Buffers.
